At Surat Thani airport, buy a coach-and-ferry combo ticket in the arrivals hall: 330–850 THB to Nathon or Lipa Noi on Koh Samui, about 3–4 hours in total, with the last combos leaving at about 16:00. Travelling independently, go to Donsak pier and take Raja Ferry to Lipa Noi (220 THB on foot, roughly hourly 05:00–19:00) or Seatran to Nathon (approx. 180–210 THB on foot). Each crossing takes about 1.5 hours.

Good to know: last checked 1 November 2026. Donsak ferry fares rose twice in March 2026 because of diesel prices, and operators change times by season. Re-check at the counter on the day. We name operators so you can find them; we do not sell their tickets.

From Surat Thani airport (URT)

Surat Thani airport is about 28 km west of Surat Thani town and about 90 minutes by road from Donsak. Low-cost airlines (Thai AirAsia, Nok Air, Thai Lion Air) fly in from Don Mueang about 12 times a day, with a few flights from Suvarnabhumi. As you leave baggage reclaim, you will see combo ticket desks. Each sells a coach or van to Donsak timed to meet its own ferry, plus the crossing.

Combos are sold on the spot, and outside peak weeks there is rarely a need to book ahead. If your flight is delayed, the desks usually move you to the next departure. Thai AirAsia also sells flight + ferry as one booking, which protects the connection if the flight is late.

Last departures: combos from URT end at about 16:00. Raja's last car ferry leaves Donsak at about 19:00. Lomprayah's last catamaran from Donsak is 15:00. Last checked 1 November 2026.

From Phun Phin railway station

Surat Thani's railway station is in Phun Phin, 14–16 km west of the town and about 80 km from Donsak. Overnight trains from Bangkok arrive between about 01:00 and 08:00; Express 85 (06:23) is the most convenient. On the station forecourt, combo sellers offer:

  • Phantip/Seatran: about 420 THB to Nathon, plus about 150 THB for a hotel drop; departures around 06:30, 07:30, 09:00 and later.
  • Raja: coaches from 05:30; the last leaves at 16:00 and reaches Lipa Noi about 20:30.
  • Lomprayah: 09:30 coach + catamaran to Nathon.
  • Boonsiri: 10:30 van from the station and town hotels for the 13:15 boat.

Allow 3.5–4 hours from the station to a Samui hotel. Trains are often 30–60 minutes late, so do not book anything tight on arrival. More on the train is in Bangkok to Koh Samui.

From Surat Thani town and the night boat

Surat Thani town has offices for Phantip and Lomprayah, and Lomprayah coaches also leave from Tapee pier (10:00 and 13:00). Buses and vans to Donsak leave from the town's bus terminals.

The old night boats from Ban Don pier in Surat Thani town are often mentioned online. In 2026 there is no regular night boat from Surat Thani to Koh Samui. Night boats from town still serve Koh Phangan and Koh Tao. If you arrive in the evening, either take the last Raja ferry from Donsak or stay overnight.

Donsak car ferries: Raja vs Seatran

Donsak, about 70 km east of Surat Thani town, is the mainland port for Samui. Raja Ferry and Seatran both run large roll-on, roll-off ferries with seating decks, snack bars and toilets. Their terminals are about 1 km apart, so make sure your driver takes you to the right one.

OperatorSamui pierCrossingFoot passengerMotorbikeCarFrequency
Raja FerryLipa Noiabout 1.5 h220 THBask at the counterask at the counterroughly hourly 05:00–19:00; extra boats late Dec–Apr
Seatran FerryNathonabout 1.5 happrox. 180–210 THBapprox. 270 THBapprox. 550–670 THB incl. driver"every hour", early morning to early evening

Seatran raised the foot fare from 170 to 180 THB on 14 March 2026, and Thai press reported a second rise in late March to 210 THB on foot, 270 THB per motorbike and 670 THB per car or pickup. Fares may come down if diesel prices fall, which is why we show ranges. Raja Ferry does not publish vehicle fares online. Seatran runs EV-only sailings on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays (05:00 from Donsak, 17:00 back), booked in advance.

Which is better?

  • Choose Raja if you are travelling early or late (it runs the longest hours) or staying on the west or south-west coast; Lipa Noi is closer to Taling Ngam, Thong Krut and Lamai's back roads.
  • Choose Seatran if you want Nathon, the island's main town with banks, songthaews and taxis waiting, or slightly lower foot fares.
  • Choose a catamaran (Lomprayah 11:00 and 15:00, Boonsiri 13:15, Songserm 16:30) if you are on foot and want the shortest crossing: 45 minutes to 1 hour for about 450 THB.

Arriving at Nathon or Lipa Noi

Nathon is Samui's administrative town on the west coast. Songthaews wait near the pier by day and run around the ring road: locals pay about 60–80 THB to Chaweng, and visitors are often asked 80–150 THB. Taxis to Chaweng cost roughly 600–1,000 THB and take 35–45 minutes; to Lamai about the same. Nathon has ATMs, a market and cafés if you need to wait. Read our Nathon guide.

Lipa Noi is a quiet stretch of the west coast a few kilometres south of Nathon. Raja's port is outside the village and songthaews are few, so most people take a taxi or a hotel transfer. Combo tickets with a "hotel drop" put you on a minibus. See our Lipa Noi area page.

If you stay on the west coast and book our boat tours, note that Lipa Noi, Nathon, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut carry a surcharge of 400 THB per person return on Chaweng-side departures. Pig Island tours leave from Thong Krut on the south coast, so south-west hotels are close to that pier. Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui.

A typical day: URT to a Chaweng hotel

  1. 08:30 Land at Surat Thani on a 07:00 flight from Don Mueang.
  2. 08:50 Collect bags and buy a combo at the arrivals desks (Raja 09:00 or Lomprayah 09:30).
  3. 09:00–10:30 Coach across the province to Donsak, about 90 minutes.
  4. 11:00 Board the catamaran or car ferry. Buy water and snacks on board.
  5. 12:00–12:30 Land at Nathon or Lipa Noi.
  6. 13:15–13:30 At your Chaweng or Lamai hotel after a 40–60 minute taxi or songthaew.

The return trip: Samui to Surat Thani

Going back, the timings tighten because you are working towards a fixed flight or train.

  • To URT for a flight: combo tickets leave the island from about 05:00 until mid-afternoon, with hotel pickup on some. Lomprayah's boat from Nathon at about 08:30 reaches URT around 11:30. Book flights departing 13:00 or later and allow 4–5 hours from a Chaweng hotel.
  • On foot to Donsak: Raja's first ferry leaves Lipa Noi at about 05:00; Seatran sails from Nathon roughly every hour.
  • To Phun Phin for a train: evening sleepers to Bangkok leave Surat Thani from late afternoon onwards; buy a combo that arrives at least 90 minutes before departure. The 09:00 daytime railcar needs a very early start.
  • Driving: on busy days, particularly Sundays and the end of Thai holidays, car queues at Nathon and Lipa Noi can mean waiting for a later boat. Arrive an hour early.

Surat Thani as a gateway

Surat Thani province includes Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, and inland Khao Sok National Park, about 2–2.5 hours west of Surat Thani by road. Raja and Seatran also sail from Donsak to Thong Sala on Koh Phangan (about 2.5 hours, Raja about 290 THB on foot), and the night boats from Surat Thani town serve Phangan and Koh Tao. Khao Sok is 4–6 hours from Samui each way, so plan an overnight stay there rather than a day trip. For Phangan and Tao from Samui, see Koh Samui to Koh Phangan and Koh Samui to Koh Tao. For the Andaman side, read Phuket and Krabi to Koh Samui.

Late arrivals and missed connections

  • Landed at URT after 16:00? Take a taxi from the airport to Donsak (about 90 minutes) for the Raja ferry. The last boat is about 19:00, so you need to leave URT by about 17:15. A private car with the ferry to your hotel costs about 6,000–9,000 THB.
  • Missed the last ferry? Donsak has a few simple guesthouses near the piers; Surat Thani town has far more hotels. Take the first Raja boat at about 05:00.
  • Coming by bus from Phuket, Krabi or Khao Sok? Through tickets usually drop you at Donsak for a specific ferry. If the bus is late, the operator normally puts you on the next sailing at no charge; keep your ticket.
  • Night train late? Combo sellers at Phun Phin run several departures each morning; you will be moved to the next one.
  • Need help on Samui? Message our local team on WhatsApp and we can suggest a transfer. [kp_wa]

Weather and sea

The Donsak–Samui crossing is sheltered compared with the open-water routes to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao. The big car ferries keep running in most weather, but the crossing gets choppy from October to December in the north-east monsoon, and services stop in tropical storms. Catamarans are more likely to be cancelled than car ferries. When Storm Pabuk hit in January 2019, all ferries were suspended. If you suffer from seasickness, sit low and in the middle of the car ferry and look at the horizon. Check conditions on our sea conditions page and the Koh Samui weather guide.

Driving yourself or bringing a rental car

Many visitors drive from Bangkok, Hua Hin or Phuket and put the car on the ferry. Seatran and Raja both take cars without advance booking in normal weeks, but queues build on Friday afternoons, around Thai public holidays and from 20 December to early January. Arrive 30–60 minutes before the sailing you want. Mainland rental contracts often exclude ferry crossings, so check yours first, or rent on the island instead. Our Koh Samui car rental guide explains insurance and the ferry clause.

Once you are on Samui

Ang Thong National Marine Park is closed from 1 November to 15 December 2026 and reopens on 16 December. From that date the Ang Thong big boat tour (1,500 THB adult, 1,100 THB child) is the best-value way to see the park. All year, our Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB adult) leaves from Thong Krut, and our private speedboat to Koh Phangan makes island hopping simple. Compare every route on how to get to Koh Samui.
